Notebook.Title: Browser Guide: Your First Live Sia Notebook

Section.Title: Start here
Section.Paragraph: This page is a live .NET workspace. Choose a notebook in the left sidebar, read from top to bottom, and press Run on a code cell whenever you want to see its output. The first run takes a little longer while the browser warms up the compiler; runs after that start quickly.

List.Item: Run compiles and executes the cell, together with any cells that share its scope.
Compile checks the same code without executing it.
Stop cancels a run or compile that is still in progress.
Save stores your edited notebook; editing a built-in creates your own copy.

Section.Paragraph: On a narrow screen, open the sidebar only when you need to switch notebooks. The editor, output, and render surfaces remain the primary work area, so zoom and text selection keep behaving like normal browser content.

Section.Title: 1. Run a cell and find its output
Section.Paragraph: Press Run below. Plain console text appears in the cell's Output view. Notebook.Render sends a value to the Render view instead. Open the cell menu if either view is hidden, then drag its tab to dock it where it is comfortable to read.

Section.Title: 2. Edit, compile, and recover
Section.Paragraph: Change the text or the number below. Use Compile first if you want diagnostics without side effects, then use Run. A diagnostic points back to the relevant source line. Discard restores the last saved source for that cell.

These three cells share Scope="browser-tour". Run any one of them and the earlier cells in the scope compile and run again first, so their types and world changes are there to use. The console above proves it — the marker entity created in the very first cell is still around when this cell replays it. Local variables never cross between cells. The scope name lives in the small field on the right of each cell's tab strip: give two cells the same name and they run together, leave it blank and the cell runs alone.

Section.Title: 3. A cell without a scope is an island
Section.Paragraph: This cell has no scope at all. Press Run and it starts from an empty world of its own — no TourMessage entities here, even though the shared scope above just created one. It declares its own copy of the type, exactly like the scoped cells do.

Section.Title: 4. Arrange the workspace

List.Item: Drag a tab by its label to move Output, Render, or editor surfaces between dock regions.
When a tab label has keyboard focus, use the arrow keys to move between neighboring tabs.
Use the cell menu to insert, move, or delete a cell; save when the layout and source are right.
Use the Packages panel only when a notebook genuinely needs an additional NuGet dependency.

Section.Paragraph: Built-in notebooks are safe starting points: saving one produces a user notebook rather than overwriting the shipped lesson. Deliberately introduce a syntax error, inspect the diagnostic, discard it, and then continue to 2. Sia Essentials.
